notes.text: OFFICIAL ARTBOOK

Since Reverse: 1999 was released, several years have passed up to today. The game's setting and tone have never stopped; instead, walking alongside all of you, they have grown and calibrated together with the tight update rhythm of every version, heading toward a more distant future. This brand-new and enduring test has once again granted us (as well as this web-like, intricately woven lore) endless vitality.

Re-exploring, collecting, and repeatedly proofreading the vast and diverse world of Reverse: 1999 was a huge challenge, yet it also allowed us to look back on that period filled with the heart's blood, talent, and youthful ideals of all the creators. Here, we sincerely invite you to turn to the next page and feel with us that surging tide of curiosity and passion.

This setting book is a gift from us to you—that legendary figure who once witnessed the roaring torrent of manus and walked against the "Storm," constantly chasing the dawn amid the tragedy—a tiny "footnote" about this world. 


— T. Tou, Game Content Director of Reverse: 1999

The "Storm" setting of Reverse: 1999 was born on a sudden, pouring night filled with the untamed, tropical wilderness atmosphere of southern China. The olive branch of fate was tossed our way—the company placed almost no creative restrictions on the project, only encouraging us to unleash our inspiration as much as possible. So, we decided to tackle a theme that hadn't appeared on the market at the time, and make a game that we ourselves would be willing to boldly explore and wholeheartedly enjoy. From that moment on, this project—carrying a simple, wild ambition—was destined to face many unexpected "firsts" and gigantic challenges.

On that blank sheet of paper holding countless possibilities of imagination, the very first things we locked down were the most practical and indispensable elements: gameplay and audience. Afterward, the world-view system, major historical chronicles, and artistic aesthetic style gradually took shape and emerged one after another as the team came together. The thematic definition of "20th-century retro occultism" step by step deduced surrealism, modern aesthetic sensibilities, cinematic texture, systematic occultism, and more—keywords that had circulated only internally. Together, they wrote the team's subconscious text and became the "lore" and "tone" we talk about every day. It was precisely these shared understandings that drove us to make, without hesitation, one decision after another that seemed uniquely independent at the time. They permeate every corner of the game: whether it is the graphic design language, the dreamy or neo-classical musical style, or even the ultimate truth revealed by the world-view—all of our oars were pulling with all their might in the exact same direction.

When it arrives, time is rendered insignificant.
Time flows back to the past, time returns to the future.
Or there is nothingness,
Or rebirth through raging fire
"Storm" Syndrome

"Storm Syndrome" is an anomalous phenomenon that occurs before a "Storm" takes place. It affects people, objects, and events, often accompanied by symptoms that drive individuals insane. The external pathological characteristics of Storm Syndrome are frequently related to the art of the era or major historical events. Under the scouring of the "Storm," the order of the world becomes unrecognizable; everything begins to trend toward madness, heading toward derivation [or proliferation]. Swallowing gold alive, craving petroleum, dancing and singing on sizzling hot iron plates. The sufferers never know they are sick—it is the same at any given time.

(1) Storm Syndrome alters the physical characteristics of victims, and sometimes changes their cognition; there is no single uniform symptom.
(2) The effects of Storm Syndrome act not only on people but also impact the environment. This influence alters the composition of the environment at a physical level.
(3) Under specific circumstances, Storm Syndrome can also affect Arcanists.

(4) Storm Syndrome does not spread worldwide immediately; instead, it starts from the "Storm" critical point and expands and intensifies along with the approaching "Storm." The closer to the critical point, the more severe the symptoms. Abnormal behaviors caused by the same syndrome may vary slightly due to regional cultural differences, but the physical manifestations—aside from the degree—are basically identical.
Asymmetric Nuclide R

A substance discovered in the raindrops of a “Storm.” It disappears very quickly after appearing and exists in an unstable state.
1.	The earliest sample of Asymmetric Nuclide R was collected by 12-year-old Vertin  during the third “Storm,” obtained directly from its raindrops.
2.	Asymmetric Nuclide R is commonly present in the atmosphere 24 hours before a “Storm” begins. During this time, enormous amounts of arcane energy are generated in the atmosphere, forming a gigantic magical array. This spiritually charged environment can overcome the bloodline restrictions normally imposed on rituals, allowing arcanists to release higher-level magic.

3.	Direct contact with unstable Asymmetric Nuclide R causes damage and deformation to hair and skin tissue.
4.	Using a sound-wave generator at a fixed frequency to stimulate Asymmetric Nuclide R can partially simulate the environment of a “Storm.”

5.	In arcanum visualization experiments, Asymmetric Nuclide R exhibits a bifurcated structure.
6.	Stable Asymmetric Nuclide R exists in the Reshaping Mask. Its immunity to “Storms” may be related to this substance.
7.	The Research Center has attempted to inject Asymmetric Nuclide R into the Balancing Mask to prevent its wearer from becoming infected with Storm Syndrome. However, this function has not yet been verified.

Social conflicts, historical changes, and the emergence of new technologies can all cause a “Storm” to occur. Human intervention can accelerate its occurrence.
After a “Storm,” the entire world undergoes an “era regression.” However, the direction of this regression is not necessarily toward the past; it may also move forward. Its underlying rules remain unknown.

The occurrence of a “Storm” goes through the following stages:
1.	Strange phenomena begin to appear.
2.	Rain falls from the sky.
3.	Signs of a Storm emerge.
4.	Rainwater begins flowing backward into the sky.
5.	The “Storm” officially occurs, and the era is “reversed.”

A phenomenon of temporal and spatial disaster, characterized by rain falling from the sky and then flowing backward into the air, causing an entire “era” to undergo a “regression.”
After a “Storm,” the world enters an “era” different from the one that existed before

A general term for the abilities and techniques that only the arcanist population can use, standing in contrast to the science created by the human race.
The most common application of arcanum is the use of arcane skills.

notes.title: Dust
notes.text: Tiny dust is nowhere to be found, yet its power is vast and incalculable. Within the powder shaken off by great beings lies the energy that triggers ascension/insight. In a certain sense, this dust is one corner of the ultimate answer
Arcanum / Occultism

notes.title: Sharpodonty
notes.text: A currency passed down from the ancient blank era to the present day, framed by twelve edges; its sharp, pointed teeth open only to those with arcane blood flowing through them

notes.title: Resonance
notes.text: Resonance is the act by which an arcanist spiritually understands and perceives existing, established things. Unlike "Inheritance," which comes from bloodline and heritage, Resonance is born purely from personal thought. An arcanist's way of thinking is primarily emotional/perceptual—that is, intuitive sensibility; a human's way of thinking is primarily rational analysis—that is, logical rationality. As for "mixed-blood arcanists" who blend human and arcanist bloodlines, those whose bloodline is still fairly normal also use "Resonance," whereas those with lower arcanist bloodline purity, as well as pure-blooded humans, use "Inspiration."

An innate talent—like the radiance in a wine cellar that will never fade.
Wondrous gifts lie hidden within the minds of arcanists, just like bloodlines or what ought to flow through their veins, often accompanied by mysterious patterns; their power varies from person to person, and their uses can be large or small—sometimes bringing convenience, and sometimes bringing long, wry smiles and irreversible trouble.

notes.title: Psychube
notes.text:
Psychube is one of the essential physiological traits of an arcanist. Even a mixed-blood individual with the smallest trace of arcanist bloodline possesses this trait.
Psychube includes two outward/manifest constants: Imaging and Amplitude.
Imaging: The impression generated by the mind—that is, an externalized image formed by different emotions, experiences, viewpoints, and thoughts. Roentgen-ray psychube detectors and crystal divination are common methods for imaging.
Amplitude: The amplitude of the psychube—that is, the wave intensity and flicker produced by psychube fluctuations. Psychube amplitude measurement is a mandatory subject in the Foundation's annual graduation exam, and Sonnetto set the highest record in this subject.

A race capable of using arcane skills; they can cast arcane skills by consuming cellular activity. This race has gradually declined, becoming progressively marginalized and forgotten after the human race grew strong.
Under the arcanist race, there are multiple subordinate branches, which are often determined by the purity and origin of their bloodline.
"A race remembered by the world for its talent, so as to be distinguished from other ordinary people. No one knows why arcanists became arcanists; they once flourished, and now have declined."

Among the descendants of humans and arcanists, individuals with a relatively diluted arcanist bloodline are called Mixed-Blood Arcanists.
There appears to be an atavistic (skip-a-generation) inheritance phenomenon, whereby an arcanist can be born into a human family that carries arcanist bloodline
Pure-blood arcanists are far stronger in their ability to use arcane skills than non-purebloods; bloodline purity and arcane skill capability have a linear relationship

Arcanists who become infected after coming into contact with Critters and transform into Infected Arcanists.

Once the transformation is complete, the subject gains the arcane abilities of the corresponding infected strain, though most die due to physical and mental collapse.

Most Awakened do not have flesh or nerves; they are merely a segment of "primordial consciousness" or motion attached to an object. Because the vessels of the Awakened are mostly non-biological matter, their lineage is often related to their composition and energy source.
Not all Awakened possess the same organs as humans; for example, Ms. Radio does not vocalize on her own, which is because she lacks vocal organs.
To facilitate movement, some Awakened attach external extension units to the core containing their primordial consciousness.
Whether the Awakened possess biological sex remains unclear, but on a cognitive level, most Awakened perceive gender as existing.
Some arcanists are born from the manifestation of cultural concepts; although these arcanists have undergone an awakening process, they do not belong to the Awakened.

Demons, blood-clan monsters, and vampiric mermaids are all categorized under the "Beyond" classification.
There exist arcanists from beyond Earth; such arcanists are often classified as Beyond.

Human ancestors are said to have been born at the exact moment the Blank Era ended; humans gradually replaced arcanists to become the dominant race.

Perception of Arcanum:
Lacking arcanist talent, humans are generally unable to interact with concepts within arcanum, though there are those among humans who understand and research arcanum.
Humans are not adept at intuitive insight, excelling instead at logical deduction based on observation.
There is a certain overlap between arcanum and human science, which allowed some arcane techniques to become the ancient predecessors of science.

A lively arcanist sports gathering originating from the Blank Era. The Games are held once a year, with the specific dates determined according to the Sacred Flame and the Uluru Games [Committee/tradition]. Comprising various specialized arcane competitive events and arcane exhibition events, it was once widely popular in the arcane world. Later, affected by the flames of war and racial antagonism, the Games vanished into history, and its ruins disappeared without a trace.
Through the cooperation of the Reincarnator Spathodea, Laplace researcher Ezra, and others, everyone found the ruins of the Games and the Sacred Flame, reviving the spirit of the Games. From this point on, the torch of the Games will be passed down year after year.

The Dushuo Festival begins on the 24th day of the twelfth lunar month  and lasts until the 15th day of the first lunar month. Among these, the 30th day of the twelfth month and the first day of the following month are New Year's Eve and the New Moon Day, when the festive atmosphere is at its richest. Every year from New Year's Eve to the first day of the first lunar month is the time when the duty gods rotate their yearly shifts and usher in the new year, which is also the origin of the people's celebrations.
Legend has it that as the passing years turn, arcanists of different Afflatuses receive a calling from the duty god of the year and are revealed their fate for the coming year. Arcanists used to hold grand celebrations at this time to bid farewell to the past and welcome new life. The celebrations, fairs, sacrifices, and prayers were magnificent in scale, and gradually, humans joined in as well.

As a general term for a class of weird creatures, "Critters" generally possess the following characteristics:
Most common Critters are small in size and exhibit behavioral traits of object mimicry, symbiosis, and adherence to customs.
Critters generally love glowing and shiny objects.
They generally show low intelligence and low aggressiveness; the Laplace Scientific Computing Center once conducted domestication experiments on Critters, proving that most Critter species have almost no possibility of intelligence improvement, though extremely rare exceptions may still exist.
Under specific conditions such as certain Critter populations or arcane influences, there is a possibility of mutation.

Common types of Critters have some overlap with the areas of humans and arcanists activities; they are weird and annoying little neighbors—pesky little creatures that occasionally cause trouble in daily life, though their attack power is usually low.

Meanwhile, large Critters that exist only in legends generally have fixed habitats and do not appear casually within human society.
Before the "Storm," anomalies reach the peak of their activity, which directly affects the behavior of Critters and increases their aggressiveness, causing them to expand their range of activity, flood into human living spaces, ruin crops, steal property, and occupy the corners where humans or arcanists are active.

Newspapers frequently publish incidents involving damage to human society, and some tabloid media are keen on spreading and reporting news about all sorts of bizarre products of out-of-control arcanists, heretical cults, and the like; after the "Storm" appeared, Critters and other arcane creatures frequently showed up in sighting incidents. In modern times, news such as "Critter Sneaks into Refrigerator at Midnight" has become countless, occupying the small corners of newspaper pages.

Aside from the utilization of a small number of Critters, the relationship between most Critters and arcanists is merely one of simple coexistence. The status of Critters among arcanists is more akin to insects or mice in the eyes of humans—mostly commensal creatures accompanying human activity (much like ants that frequently appear in houses). Of course, they can have other uses, and they are neither rare nor precious, appearing with no great frequency in human or arcanist settlements. Some Critters also hold value as food or for fulfilling certain functions, and most arcanists are able to accept eating Critters.

notes.title: The Pax House
notes.text: The Pax Security Council (Human Peace and Security Council)

You have certainly heard of that snow-white stone house suspended high above. The textbooks tell us that it is the Pax Security Council, the current supreme governing body of Earth. They do not directly manage human society, appearing only at critical moments concerning survival and development.

The Pax House seems to possess the ability to use pigeons for surveillance and transmitting messages. These white pigeons composed of plaster are called "the pigeons of the white stone house" by high-ranking officials in the know.
An organization under the Pax Security Council, an international body responsible for the discovery, containment, management, and utilization of arcanists, arcane items, and the like.

"Within a quarter of an hour after the silver bell rings, loyal companions stand lined up here in waiting. A peacekeeping organization active around the world, and the container and manager of arcanists, arcane items, and arcane phenomena. You can safely entrust your child to the St. Pavlov Foundation; he will become a good child here."

The St. Pavlov Foundation is an international organization with the Joint Committee at its core, establishing the Communion Faction and other departments as well as subordinate agencies beneath it, with branches and affiliated offices built in various regions. Subordinate agencies include field organizations such as the Outsourced Contract Talent Management Organization, the School of Primary Defense serving as an educational institution, the Night Watch Special Operations Management Bureau responsible for preventing and investigating arcanist criminal cases, and the Timekeeper Squad which holds an independent establishment.

1. The Foundation is dedicated to safeguarding the human world and promoting social relations between arcanists and human groups, though internal attitudes and views on this differ.
2. The organization is committed to discovering, containing, and utilizing the world's remaining arcane power; the occurrence of the "Storm" has made this duty even more vital.
3. "May peace be with us, may peace be with mankind" is the Foundation's fundamental creed; the Peace Declaration based on this creed states that "regardless of physical health, wealth or poverty, or racial differences, one should extend a helping hand to maintain Earth's peaceful order."
4. The Foundation's guiding policy is to implement the "Peace Policy" and promote the integration of arcane technology into human society. Every year, the Foundation incurs massive expenditures for arcanum-related culture and education.
5. The Foundation restricts arcanists through discipline and control; some members believe that malignant incidents in history stemmed from the restless nature of arcanists, and therefore controls cannot be relaxed.
6. Numerous ideologies and factions exist within the Foundation; the contradictions in their demands and beliefs are fracturing the Foundation's convictions, and after the "Storm" occurred, factions such as human supremacism began to rise.
In accordance with the "Containment Management Regulations," the St. Pavlov Foundation registers and manages arcanists of various risk levels, and strives to promote integration between races.

One of the subordinate agencies of the St. Pavlov Foundation, providing education for underage arcanists and using specific educational methods to enhance students' understanding of arcanum, helping them form sound and reliable values. More than half of its graduating students go on to serve in the Foundation, mostly as frontline investigators.

1. In certain respects, the Foundation intentionally restricts staff members' awareness of the "Storm.
2. The Foundation conceals the existence of the "Storm" from the masses of each era through methods including, but not limited to, controlling the media, and only screens specific candidates of value.
3. The "Storm" is a strictly forbidden term within the School of Primary Defense under its jurisdiction; students who mention it receive detention, while staff members are escorted away.

1. The "Storm" emergency system was established after the second "Storm." Proposed by Lucy, the head of Laplace at the time, and jointly built with the Foundation, the system includes the following steps:
-Establish contact with all branches in the current era and tally deployable manpower.
-Establish observation stations worldwide to search for other areas immune to the "Storm."
-Establish multiple workshops to deduce the causes of the "Storm."

2. After the third "Storm," the Foundation established the Timekeeper to provide authoritative reports and records of outside time.
3. Because social conflicts, historical turmoil, the birth of new technologies, and other factors can trigger or accelerate the "Storm," the Foundation assigned outsourced contract teams the duty of forecasting the "Storm's" tipping point—a duty distinct from that of dispatched investigators.
4. During the ninth "Storm," the Scientific Computing Center developed "Storm"-immune protective gear—the Equilibrium Umbrella. Some senior investigators are issued samples, while others can obtain an Equilibrium Umbrella through application.

1. The Foundation has established corresponding processing standards and containment procedures for "Storm" survivors.
2. After a "Storm," the Foundation arranges new era-appropriate identities for headquarters staff and dispatches investigators to collect arcane materials, equipment, preservable arcane skills, and high-level technical talent from that era based on retained records.
3. Before a "Storm" occurs, field personnel are ordered to abandon their missions and return to headquarters for shelter. Before taking shelter, they must undergo an inspection procedure to screen for the effects of "Storm" syndrome; those severely affected by "Storm" syndrome are quarantined and have their movements restricted.
4. Given the limited space at headquarters, unregistered non-essential personnel, including family members, are prohibited from entering headquarters.
5. During the "Storm" countdown, the Foundation conducts an internal inventory of its preserved era collections and historical records.

An identification badge obtained by Foundation members upon formal onboarding. With this ID card, one can enter and exit areas permitted by their rank. If the ID card is lost, a loss report must be submitted before going through the replacement process.
A passport-like pass carried by Foundation field personnel. The basic information on this credential differs from an ID card, displaying only job title, name, and signature.

A specialized communicator issued to Foundation field personnel with diverse functions, capable of communication, enemy detection, and identifying abnormal fluctuations in surrounding arcane skills. Different functions are unlocked based on the user's clearance level.

Chess is Constantine's most beloved sport; she excels at it just as she is well-versed in the art of power and politics
On the final day of 1999, the "Storm" washed away nearly everything, replaced by foolish despair and ignorance. A chessboard named Fate unfolded amidst the recklessly backward-flowing time, and within it lay the very moment requiring someone to hold the pieces.
As the final piece fell, she saw that the people had become pure white chess pieces, their faces filled with youthfulness, crimson blood... they served as part of something grand, as the price to be paid.

During our creative process, Constantine was conceived as Vertin's antithesis. She is a thorough political creature; years of political experience have made her adept at weighing the value behind every emotion. To her, only by fathoming others' emotions without exposing oneself can one effortlessly control the situation.

Constantine has always believed the Foundation is overly tolerant toward arcanists—they are uncontrollable, manic, and disorderly. Yet the Foundation not only accommodates these flaws, it dotes upon these people. While the outside world may harbor prejudices against arcanists, years of political experience make Constantine far more inclined to view this as an opportunity.

Constantine's symbolic motif is the white lily.
Codename Z

Her real name is Zhang Zhizhi, but the character "之" in her name was mistakenly read as "Z" by the British. Following the trend of studying abroad, the outstanding student Z chose to study at Imperial College London, hoping to return home and contribute to her family's development. Due to her exceptional scientific achievements and research into the arcane, Z successfully received an invitation from the foundation. From then on, this bright figure moved tirelessly between gray and white buildings, striving for her ideals and her eventual return to her homeland

"Ambitious young lady who went abroad to study in response to the trend of studying abroad, and who came from engineering disciplines"—this was our initial idea when we created Ms. Zhang Zhizhi. You can find a certain lingering charm of "gentleness, kindness, respect, frugality, and humility" in her, but for us, equally important is the sharpness hidden beneath that gentleness. Carrying a thermos all year round, keeping jasmine tea bags on her desk, and not drinking unboiled water—these kinds of quirks always arouse the curiosity and learning of her colleagues.

She was free from self-interest or partisan political prejudice, which earned her widespread popularity among different factions within the St. Pavlov Foundation. She argued vehemently for her ideals and initiatives, yet disregarded the slander and defamation of certain interest groups.
In her brief few years at the Foundation, she has set foot in the School of Primary Defense, the Laplace Scientific Computing Center, the Zeno Armaments Academy, and more; she conversed happily with the still-young intern registrar, Laplace researchers, and Foundation committee members. She grew up fast—so fast that even her former ideals could not keep pace with her footsteps. Although we may have regrettably lost a great physicist, perhaps we are able to welcome a true politician.

Full name Greta Hofmann, a dispatched investigator from Germany and an anthropologist. She holds a firm conviction in the Foundation's ideal of "advancing the progress of all humanity." Hofmann is the older sister of Laplace researcher Enigma; she frequently writes letters to Enigma, sharing the world after the "Storm."

Hofmann is a protagonist of the main story special chapter "The Star"; we sought to interpret and witness this disaster through the perspective of an ordinary human investigator of the Foundation. Thus, Hofmann carries both the radiance of human rationality and the despair when rationality faces the collapse of order, as well as the selflessness and courage to still choose to shoulder responsibility after despair.
Hofmann and Enigma, this sister and brother, serve as foils to one another; both are loyal to their inner rationality and principles. Although they share the same beliefs and are both willing to strive for them, they truly lacked communication, to the point of causing misunderstandings between family members. (Yet both firmly believe in the strength of their bond!)
The story of "E lucevan le stelle" was actually created before "The Star"; in Version 1.7 she appeared as a "been-there-done-that" mentor, whereas the special chapter revealed a softer, more emotional, and more lost side of her youth. ("The Star" pays homage to Arthur C. Clarke's short story of the same name.)
Hofmann is German, yet she also possesses a certain quirky sense of humor, even though it is unintentional. Hofmann can always see through Marcus's problems at a glance and point out their essence. At the same time, however, she indulges her student; hoping that Marcus can grow in an arcanist's way that better suits her own nature, she offers only rational, limited advice.

A scientific research institution under the Pax Security Council; through a research and development direction that combines human technology and arcanum, it is dedicated to research that enables humans to use arcane technology.

"All things have cause and effect, and the world returns to unity. Aiming to deeply research future technology as well as the integration of technology and arcane skills, providing possibilities for the development of arcanum and humanity. The Scientific Computing Center rose to prominence during the course of several industrial revolutions, and its current primary goal is to propel the arrival of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR)."

Laplace employees' identification documents include formal employee badges and temporary badges for interns. These badges grant the holder specific authority and allow access to areas permitted by their job duties.

Compared to early hypnotherapy, Artificial Somnambulism technology allows the user to enter a deep hypnotic state. Through auditory stimulation and guidance, it directionally induces reactions such as imagination, memories, and emotions.

-During Artificial Somnambulism, certain specific fragments from past memories can activate trauma fragments, leading to treatment failure.
-In addition to hypnotherapy, Artificial Somnambulism technology can also be used for combat simulation, training, and assessment. These functions require the user to perform specific physical movements to activate on the machine. The simulated combat function allows multiple people to train simultaneously and can increase training difficulty.

notes.title: Currently known simulation programs for Artificial Somnambulism include:

notes.text:
-Once Artificial Somnambulism begins, the user feels "an invisible fluid being blocked," after which simulated scenes appear in their field of vision.
-Artificial Somnambulism technology is also used to manufacture weapons; some of the Foundation's guard captains are equipped with weapons produced via Artificial Somnambulism.

An item used by Foundation personnel to store and cast arcane skills. Materialized incantations that have been thoroughly mastered can be stored inside it. Different incantations require floppy disks made of different materials for storage.

-Developed by the Scientific Computing Center to collect samples of Asymmetric Nuclide R, designed specifically for its property of rapidly vanishing without a trace.
-If the test-paper tube inside the device turns gold after absorbing a sample, it indicates that Asymmetric Nuclide R has been collected. The speed of color change corresponds to the concentration of Asymmetric Nuclide R in the sample.

notes.title: "Storm"-immune protective gear developed by the Scientific Computing Center; its structure consists of the following three parts:
notes.text:
-—Ritual Core: A materialized ritual of the "Storm"-immunity incantation (i.e., the Hoffman Knot). It prevents the user from being reversed, though it is limited by cases where the user's spiritual capacity is insufficient to meet casting requirements, as well as curse side effects.
-—Converter: Improved from X's Equilibrium Headpiece technology, it can generate an equilibrium field from the atmosphere filled with arcane energy prior to the "Storm," allowing the user to meet the casting conditions.
-—Harmonizer: Its totem originates from the Equilibrium Scroll, utilizing its property of "bridging the spiritual chasm" to neutralize curse effects.
As it is still in the testing phase, the first-generation Equilibrium Umbrella can only effectively prevent 162 types of side effects.

A radical arcane organization composed of arcanists, many of whose members hold pure-blood supremacist ideologies; the organization's core objective is to return to an era when the arcanist race was prosperous and the order was right.

"By our hands, we reshape your order." They emerge from the pitch-black mire, fearless of the scouring rain, expanding and growing at a terrifying pace. Wielding power and influence, they reshape all things; the world grants their noble blood the authority that is rightfully theirs. They come for revival, and they also come for vengeance—that banner belonging to the arcane arts and their inheritors shall one day fly high atop the tallest beacon in the world.

Manus Masks can effectively prevent the wearer from contracting "Storm" syndrome, but cannot guarantee that the wearer will not be affected by the "Storm's" reversal.
Once the mask is put on, unknown arcane skills will be awakened.
Manus Masks inflict contamination upon the wearer, which includes causing the wearer's thoughts to become extreme, losing sanity, and the like. The more powerful the mask, the more numerous and severe the hidden side effects of mental contamination, with the possibility of irreversibility; there have been instances of wearers completely losing their sanity and going berserk.
One bestowed with an arcane sacred icon by Lady Arcana, a witness to the Passion, a messenger of the divine oracle, and a servant of the "Resurrection".
The sole revered figure within Manus Vindictae, a prophet, and one who guides people onto the right path.
High-ranking members who have passed the Manus trials; unlike Believers and Disciples, Apostles retain their own will and often hold devout faith in the Master.
Lacking a self and acting autonomously, disciples who possess a pure faith. They possess a unique mode of communication—a language understood only by Manus members, written using phonetic symbols
The most basic-level followers of Manus Vindictae; their bodies undergo physical transformation due to the influence of Manus Masks, mostly merging with characteristics of hybrid beasts.
All adherents of Manus Vindictae; their outward appearance is no different from ordinary people, except that they wear Manus Masks.

-Manus Vindictae aims to revive arcanum. Manus Vindictae believes the organization holds the authority to rewrite all things, and attempts to use the "Storm" to turn back the era and reach that "past with the right order."
-Manus Vindictae is an Arcanist organization opposed to humans. They advocate preserving a pure arcanist bloodline, and therefore generally do not accept Mixed-Blood Arcanists.
-Manus Vindictae holds a friendly attitude toward pure-blood arcanist organizations and will provide assistance such as survival supplies to the other party when necessary, though these "good deeds" do not stem entirely from goodwill.

-"Blood and flesh" are terms commonly used by Manus members regarding their faith; they believe that their blood and flesh are shared with their compatriots.
-After being slain, Arcana became the "Suffering One." Followers believe that the Guide will take fate into their own hands and choose to suffer in place of the faithful, and that they will be reborn from the dust to avenge every inch of land tread upon. The followers of Manus Vindictae will become one with them once again and return to the golden age.
-Manus Vindictae holds trials, including the Mask Trial, to screen followers and test the loyalty of newcomers.

-An ancient ritual that allows the user to pass through the "Storm."
-The incantation uses a language system that is both from 1999 and unknown, reading "La Unua Cirklo."
-The Immunity Ritual is a "high-tier arcane skill"; bloodline purity limitations can prevent the caster from meeting the casting requirements.

-This ritual can incur curse side effects of many varieties, most of which are related to "earth" and "dust."
-The effects of the curse on the awakened differ from other arcanists. The side effect is damage to the outer shell while leaving the core essence intact; damage to the core often manifests as memory loss.
-here is roughly a 0.49% chance that no curse will occur.
-Due to humans' inability to use arcane skills, forcibly reading the incantation text will not take effect.

Wearing the Mask: All followers must put on a Manus Mask. It will shelter them beneath the "Storm," freeing their minds from the restraint of ordinary sanity and amplifying the arcane energy of the soul, without being bound by sanity, morality, or reason.
-Undergoing the Test: The mask will test whether you possess what's needed to join the Manus; even the slightest fluctuation of the mind or action will be captured by the boundless arcanum.
-Accepting the Curse or the Blessing: You become a blessed follower, or conversely, a believer forever cursed amidst wailing.

notes.title: Trial II · Trial of the Elect

notes.text:
-Brain Sacrifice: Draw your brain matter out from your temples and place it upon the twin sacrificial trays of the sacred statue's hands. Your brain is soothed by these warm palms.
-Supreme Faith: A choice of one out of three faith missions.
The Choice of Zeal: Infiltrate human communities and use arcane abilities to complete tasks of investigation, persuasion, and control. 
Trial of Loyalty: Venture into the shadows of the Temple of the Manus Vindictae, where the unbelievers of the Manus Vindictae are imprisoned. They are cunning, shameful, and hypocritical humans. Purify and judge them! Atone for the arcane's original glory with your blood. 
Trial of Piety: Confront humanity's evil and hypocrisy, and resist the seduction of their words. Bring along a human companion whom you despise or whom you deeply love, and offer them to the benevolent Goddess. Their soul will be purified within the temple and attain true eternal existence.
-Accept the curse or the blessing: You become a blessed chosen one, exalted to the rank of a glorious apostle, a holy anonymous one. Those who fail the trial will either become a disciple forever cursed amidst wailing, or face a merciful death with their brains crushed.

Cast off sanity—those pale parasites clinging to your skin for thousands of years. They drain your spirit and spiritual aura, bringing only ever-increasing restraints and pain; no one pays heed to your talent and gifts, and only the benevolent Arcane Mother will free you from cold, ruthless shackles.

Look directly at the lies—inborn talent became the excuse for your clan's slaughter, yet you were born of blessing, a benevolent soul nurtured by inspired chanters. Everything you had was once taken away and torn apart, leaving endless pain. Bow down and sit still; the Mother will admonish you on what is false and draw in all your sorrows; what awaits you is a comforted heart and endless grace in the days to come.

Unleash your senses—you are no longer bound by shackles and lies. You no longer stir at the temptation of false material things. You offer countless lives as sacrifice to the Guide, and she shall repay you ten millionfold, blessing you with an incomparable arcane talent, amplifying your keen insight, and letting the micro-vibrations of all things in the world awaken a supreme storm of bliss.

Arcana is the center of Manus Vindictae's faith, while also holding an important place in the beliefs of many in the arcane world, and thus bears many aliases and identities. Appellations such as "The Guide," "The Sufferer," "Arcane Mother," and "Mother of Rsurection" ultimately all point to this mysterious lady. She bestows miracles and promises salvation, yet few know the motives behind these gifts.

Arcana is a pure villain character; for the story, we needed to confront an enemy like this—She must be mysterious enough, dangerous enough, and seemingly invincible. Yet if it were only that, it would seem hard to imagine in what guise she would descend upon the world.
After long, passionate discussions, we finally decided to link Her with the most obvious and visible characteristic of this world, namely "flow."
 Thus, a "woman" with a simple yet sophisticated design walks gracefully towards us. Her steps are gentle and elegant, and an indescribable viscous substance condenses into a river behind her. (We must admit that after reaching an agreement, most of us felt a similar mix of trepidation and excitement.) 
With Manus Vindictae finding its master, the concept and art direction for this faction could finally be settled logically. Thanks to Arcana, the members of Manus Vindictae all have excellent taste in clothing. 
Unfortunately, we cannot reveal any more about Lady Arcana (let's call her Lady for now). Firstly, we wish to maintain a degree of mystery before you experience the story firsthand; secondly, attempting to discuss unspeakable matters might invite…

Born into the Cavendish family, a clan renowned for its potion-making and rare cork trade, Forget Me Not was another rare potion-making genius in the family. Sadly, however, he failed to lead this ancient family to new heights, unlike previous prodigies. A multi-faceted conspiracy destroyed his future, his family's future, and the futures of countless relatives and friends, both older and younger than him. In that wisp of ashes known as Cavendish, a cold, sinister snake hissed and disappeared into the distance.

The Jazz Age arrived alongside Prohibition—vibrant, thriving, restless—with the sky-devouring flames of desire hanging over the New York dome together with the golden sunset, as if night would never come. Where is the American Dream? The American Dream is right here. 
Yes, the creative inspiration behind Forget Me Not stems from this—Francis Scott Key Fitzgerald's 1925 novel The Great Gatsby.

Building upon the broader backdrop of the Jazz Age and the Great Depression, how about telling a story of a commoner rising into high society? That is a classic American Dream, isn't it? Or, how about a story of an aristocrat falling into the common ranks? That would surely be interesting as well. Thus, in Forget Me Not, you can see the shadows of both kinds of people. It is as if this character himself carries a retrospective gaze, allowing us to examine that dazzling, decadent era through his eyes: shifts in class, arcanists and humans struggling in such an environment, all beauty ultimately turning to foam, and bodies turned into money crashing into mire on Wall Street.

From a typical Italian family from Sicily—impoverished and destitute, yet immensely devout in their faith. Schneider is the youngest child in the family. After immigrating to Chicago, she adapted very well here, managing a gang, taking part in shady dealings, and leading her parents and twelve older sisters out of poverty.
Feathers named responsibility, sin, and freedom are stitched onto her dress piece by piece; beneath them is wrapped a light, unrestrained free spirit.

We attempt to recreate, through Schneider's initial role as a "flapper girl", the young women of the Roaring Twenties in the West who pursued individuality and independence, rejecting the harsh constraints of society. They embraced androgynous short hair, wore clothing that combined allure and playfulness, scorned rules and constraints, and were indifferent to everything. (Yes, recognizable and captivating bad girls!)

Being a flapper is part of Schneider, shaping the Schneider of Chicago. Yet our girl obviously wasn't born in Chicago; she came from the orange groves of Sicily, a poor, simple rural soil. We were all certain that the future Schneider would be a mysterious hitwoman or a gang boss—someone who could raise a gun and willingly gather her older sisters and parents behind her. Before that, however, she was still just the youngest child in the family. Once we uncovered these traits belonging solely to her, this somewhat precocious "flapper" finally stepped gracefully onto our stage.
Remember her; at this moment, you too, just like us, are trying to reach out and catch this light feather lifted upon a tender yet rebellious wave of fashion.

An arcanist group born out of Pythagoreanism and concealed on a small island in the Aegean Sea. The school aims to investigate the truth of the world's essence and holds the value system that all things are number.
"All things are number. Abstraction is the essence of the world, and all truth is abstract, pure, and transcendental. The phenomenal world is impure, material, and enslaved by desire. Human souls will continuously reincarnate in the world, forming a cycle. Follow the doctrine, purify the soul, and become one with the world of ideas."

An arcane artifact used by the Apeiron school to enforce oaths. It requires both parties taking the oath to carve their names onto the bracelet and offer a single drop of fresh blood for the artifact to take effect.
Theoretically impossible to remove. If an oath is broken within the bounds of the Apeiron sanctuary, the bracelet grows scorching hot as a warning; in severe cases, rumor has it that it drinks the oath-breaker's blood as punishment. It is widely used to suppress hostility and conflict.
Responsible for examining/discussing social issues.

Possesses the Soul Number "6," inherits the memories of previous leaders, and is regarded as the successor/heir of Pythagoras. "6" bears the mission of guarding the gate leading to the Apeiron (the Unlimited).
Specializes in inquiry, speculation, and dialectical reasoning.
Responsible for maintaining order and advancing the smooth conduct of Citizen Assembly votes.
Responsible for doctrinal affairs and related activities.
Specializes in the study of the natural world.

-Error-Corrector:Within the Apeiron school, specializes in verifying massive volumes of calculations in order to eliminate errors in computation. Beyond eliminating errors in calculations and proofs, minor tasks such as untangling loose threads and smoothing out creases also fall within their scope of error-purging.
-Applicant: Members who have not yet formally entered the Apeiron school.
-Silent One: Applicants who are permitted entry must swear an oath of strict secrecy.
-Auditor: Outside visitors permitted to attend sermons/lectures, who must observe the same rules of silence and secrecy as the Silent Ones. They serve as the school's primary bridge for external outreach and fundraising.

Members of the Apeiron school are composed of arcanists.
Preachers must strictly observe a set of precepts and a way of life in order to suppress the madness in their bloodline and maintain the island's arcanum.
School members and visitors wear arcane robes of a uniform style but in different colors according to their rank.
Among them, the lowest-ranking "Auditors" wear black robes and must maintain silence and secrecy.

notes.title: Overview of Precepts
notes.text:
▲Ancient Taboos: Vegetarianism; abstaining from beans; not touching a white rooster; entering the temple from the right and exiting from the left; not poking fire with a sword or blade; not jumping over a yoke; not sitting on a measuring vessel; not separating bread; not picking up something after it drops; prohibiting entering the assembly hall wearing brand-new clothes that have never been worn; not having swallows in a room; not sleeping within sacred walls; rolling up one's bedding upon leaving it; smoothing out the imprints left by sleeping; and not disturbing another person while they are witnessing.
▲Eating beans is the most severe of all taboos; violating this taboo directly incurs grave punishment. Furthermore, consuming a creature that has eaten beans carries the exact same offense.

notes.title: Lifestyle Requirements
notes.text:
▲Morning: Rise with Apollo's star (the sun), recall the deeds and events of the previous day, and quietly meditate on the tasks to be done today. This is to ensure that one's memory receives the finest exercise. Afterward, take a walk in the fields. Return to the hall to attend lectures, followed by washing the body, engaging in physical exercise, and eating breakfast—consuming only slices of bread spread with honey.
▲Daytime: Handle communal chores and engage in discussions on academic questions.
▲Dusk: Take a final walk, during which everyone helps one another recall the teachings received that day.
▲Evening: After bathing, gather together and dine ten to a table. Once the meal is finished, the youngest member reads aloud a classic essay or poem. Then hold a communal prayer to conclude the day's activities. Everyone returns to their own quarters to carry out the final introspection of the day, examining every action and every word from that day.

▲Their beliefs originate from Pythagoreanism, wherein the term "Apeiron" means "the Unlimited" (or "the Boundless"), the origin of all things. The world came into being through the division of the "Unlimited" by the "Limited." The manifestation of this division is mathematics, which exists within all things as the most primordial "arcane" rhythm—and thus, all things are number.
▲The school holds that the essence of the world is abstract, termed the World of Ideas or the Transcendental World, and is therefore pure and transcendental. The phenomenal world—that is, the material world—is impure and enslaved by desire. Every person has been exiled from the World of Ideas into the phenomenal world. The soul undergoes continuous reincarnation, and believers must follow the doctrine to purify their souls, ultimately merging back into the abstract World of Ideas.

▲Apeiron preachers attain gnosis (spiritual knowledge) through spirituality to seek out the origins of arcanum and investigate the truth of the world's essence. Believers hold that mathematics is the very essence of arcanum. Spreading gnosis is the school's way of propagating its ideals.
▲The ultimate proposition of the Apeiron school can be understood as the search for truth—namely, transcendental laws. Meanwhile, the notion that "the world of essence is irrational" is the school's greatest taboo.
▲In the understanding of the Apeiron school, the "Storm" is referred to as the "Emanation" (Spiritual Overflow) or "Spiritual Surge." They believe that the "Emanation" is a tide of spirituality—the manifestation of abstract essence within the phenomenal world, serving to purify the world. The school views the sanctuary's survival through the "Emanation" as salvation and a divine mission, believing that by discovering its patterns, one can reach the World of Ideas.

Sophia was brought to the island in her childhood by her engineer father. She is a talented arcanist child, yet within this school that reveres numbers, she is unremarkable. Her perception of numbers is ordinary, so she can only rely on hard work, arduous study, and rigorous calculation in an attempt to catch up with the terrifying pace of her peer, 37. This pressure tempered her, and at the youngest age on record, she took on the role of the school's Error-Purger—responsible for verifying and checking for errors in massive volumes of calculations.

Following the creation of 37, the second Apeiron character to be born was Sophia. At the very inception of creating Sophia, we had already determined her Soul Number. Irrational numbers to irrationality, mathematical crisis to the spiritual crisis of the 20th century, the disillusionment of the digital/numerical paradise to the shift from the classical to the modern. Starting from Plato's allegory and ultimately reflecting the zeitgeist of the 20th century—this was the nested structure established from the very beginning.
Compared to 37, who acts as a "priestess" bringing revelations, we wanted Sophia to be a devout "defender of the faith/orthodoxy." She believes she is fighting for the truth—that as long as she fulfills her duties and holds fast to the right convictions, the truth will arrive, even if it is a truth brought by others.
The island is rife with contradictions born of identity and self-betrayal: the Leader of the school possesses no faith, the priestess who illuminates the truth proves nothingness, and the "Error-Purger" proves that she herself is an error. This reflects the historical conflicts of the Pythagorean school, a Greek-style paradox, and humanity's struggle in the face of fate. Yet heroic will is made manifest precisely through fighting back against fate. In "The Prisoner in the Cave", there were allegorical correspondences for the characters: 6 is Oedipus, 37 is Achilles, and 210 is Icarus, yet Sophia was not among them—she is no hero, but an ordinary person awaiting salvation.
The fate of Sophia of the Apeiron school was sealed from the start. As for Sophia of Manus Vindictae, it is still too early to speak of her here—let us look forward to the next stage.

Within the Apeiron school, 210 was an all-around genius who stood out at a young age; blessed with a photographic memory and keen dialectical reasoning, virtually no one ever defeated him in a debate. He could quickly grasp the crux of any field, yet he specialized in none. As time passed, those who had once lost to him all found fields to delve deeply into—and that perpetually taciturn classmate whom he had disdained even became the Leader of the school. Yet 210 remains carefree and unrestrained, indulging in verbal victories and grandiloquent talk.

notes.title: Behind-the-Scenes Perspective
notes.text:
Like 6, 210 is also a character who took shape as the story progressed, yet he immediately stole the spotlight the moment he appeared—because he talks so much.
210's identity draws reference from Greek "rhetoricians" (sophists) and skilled debaters, while his visual design draws inspiration from Dionysus, the god of wine. He is a pivotal character reflecting the core themes of the story: if there is no truth, then everything is mere rhetoric; if faith in truth collapses, one can only turn toward aesthetic indulgence. Yet 210 has not accepted this spiritual crisis—his four consecutive prime factors  allow him to comprehend the truth of nothingness, yet not a single one of these four equally matched, admirable numbers can point him in the right direction. Herein lies his contradiction. Thus, we see him playing with rhetoric while declaring that rhetoric is meaningless; urging others to indulge in revelry while claiming he acts for the sake of truth. He refuses to accept the void, yet he is already helplessly standing right in the midst of it. And so, he drinks, cries out, and drains the fine wine in his cup.
210 is adept at uttering remarks that sound flattering at first listen, yet are actually subtly sarcastic. Unfortunately, the people on the island are far too familiar with his shtick—so much so that whenever he starts praising someone, the Integers always impatiently tell him to hurry up and get to the second half. —Had he been outside the island, he would undoubtedly have achieved great things.

An organization under the Human Peace and Security Council (HPSC) aimed at cultivating and integrating arcanist and human military talent. While carrying out cooperative projects across various regions, it expands the influence of the Pax House.

"Obedient, resolute, and never flinching. Combining strength with strength, it is an organization that advocates merging the armed forces of the arcane world with the armed forces of human society. Operating across the globe as the Pax House's standing army, it simultaneously shoulders the responsibility of screening and cultivating the next generation of combat forces. Following the signing of the Horizon Convention, it successively signed cooperation agreements with various nations, taking in individuals of eligible age from different countries to undergo systematic tactical training."

As a subordinate body under the Human Peace and Security Council, Zeno takes maintaining peace and preventing chaos as its mission. Zeno has stations in various regions to assist in preserving order, and oversees a Disaster Relief Offices to carry out humanitarian aid.

notes.title: Zeno's Education
notes.text:
Recruitment:
Each year, Zeno releases  admissions test questions, and anyone who signs their name can enter the assessment. The test simulates battlefield conditions.

Training:
Zeno conducts survival simulation exams in which the operating area continuously shrinks. Zeno also holds regular military exercises. During exercises, participating cadets are divided into two opposing groups, and whether they can execute the drill according to the combat plan is factored into their exercise evaluation. According to statistics, personnel washed out each year for failing assessments account for roughly 4% of the total.

The editorial department of the magazine "UTTU," founded and edited/published by White Pine. Members of the editorial department communicate and share intelligence by catching wind of rumors/news, scattered across the world in search of everything worth recording.

"A renowned magazine well-known to both the mundane world and the Arcanum world. A magazine covering lifestyle, news, history, art, fashion, and Arcanum dispatches. What you want to know, what you don't want to know, the public and the non-public—you can see it all right here."

notes.title: Department Structure
notes.text: The UTTU Editorial Department once had three editorial divisions working in coordination: the Text-Weaving Department, the Information-Gathering Department, and the Photography and Scent-Analysis Department. However, with the emergence of The Storm and staff reductions, this departmental structure has gradually faded away.

notes.title: Organizational Beliefs
notes.text:
The magazine’s unique name and logo are said to be related to a being called “Uttu”.

The magazine upholds the view that "people can be works of art—whether dead or alive," and records information about interviewees based on dimensions such as "fragrance, size, and medium." Capturing and perceiving the flowing wind is the core of the interview activities; therefore, the editorial office does not have a fixed location.

notes.title: The Spider's Shared Web
notes.text: The network, composed of invisible and ubiquitous threads, links the magazine editors together. The ability to hear the wind has also endowed the editorial staff with special sensory abilities; they are said to be able to sense approaching "storms" and even perceive places to take shelter from them.

notes.title: She watched the future slip away in a flash,
The world of yesterday comes roaring in.

notes.text: Timekeeper is a post under the St. Pavlov Foundation. Vertin became the Timekeeper after the third occurrence of The Storm, meaning the one who records the birth and disappearance of "eras." The Timekeeper is the sole authoritative recorder and reporter of time for the Foundation. Foundation personnel must rely on the Timekeeper's observations to confirm the moment to which The Storm has reversed. Because of the ability to move freely within The Storm, the Timekeeper bears the duty of issuing evacuation notices 24 hours before The Storm.

According to the "Field Mission Evacuation Instructions", anyone facing difficulties within 24 hours prior to The Storm may seek assistance from the Timekeeper.

After the seventh Storm, the Timekeeper's duties expanded to spearheading investigations concerning The Storm and Manus Vindictae.
Following the passage of the "The Storm Reformation: Manpower and Discipline " motion, the Timekeeper gained the following powers and responsibilities:
External personnel recruited by the Timekeeper are placed within the Timekeeper's establishment. The Timekeeper provides unified instruction, supervision, and control, and is responsible for their subsequent conduct."

All Arcanists incorporated into the Timekeeper's establishment must uniformly undergo the Foundation's risk assessment and be classified into tiers based on the results. Ordinary Arcanists only need to attend elementary artificial somnambulism training. More anomalous Arcanists must be sent to a reformatory school for study."
"Personnel within the Timekeeper's establishment, on the premise of abiding by the 'Foundation Employee Code of Conduct,' are accountable to the Timekeeper's orders and need not take orders directly from the Foundation."

The Timekeeper's team has an independent budget and establishment, and may borrow personnel from the St. Pavlov Foundation, the Laplace Computing Center, and Zeno Arms Academy. Disciplinary authority over unregistered Arcanists belongs to the Foundation.
Ms. Z serves as the liaison between the Timekeeper's team and the Foundation. The Timekeeper may independently formulate investigation objectives and plans regarding The Storm and Manus Vindictae, and report periodically to the Foundation.

"I promise, I will never sneak a peek at the outside scenery again!
The slumbering forest so still it looks black, the pale water surface and reefs, and the hawks and white doves snatching food between the cliffs and marble—none of them are appealing! What's more, there are no iron railings or pungent spray out beyond the perimeter wall to protect us; who knows if there might be something out there ten thousand times scarier than the rumbling monster in the ventilation duct of the fifth storage room...!
Before that, I ought to become a brave investigator.
Just like those free, diverse gentlemen and ladies hurrying through the off-white houses between the dense fog and the forest, standing tall with backs as straight and firm as pure white walls. Though I'm nearly forgetting their faces—were they French, Swedish, English, Australian, Portuguese...? Never mind, that is how our future is meant to look anyway. Ah, how elegant, how enchanting—"

Dear teacher, upon reading this, I imagine you must be moved by a well-behaved child who has truly reformed, and perhaps you're even itching to give me a hug—but please don't! This is Charles's masterpiece. The punishment in the detention room has effectively trained him, and I only offered him three hazelnuts in exchange for this letter of repentance. However, out of respect for intellectual property rights, I'm willing to give him all the rewards you originally planned…^_^

                                           —— Vertin

However, out of respect for intellectual property rights, I'm willing to give him all the rewards you originally planned…^_^

                                           —— Vertin

An Arcanum artifact/prop carried by Vertin that allows living beings such as Arcanists and Critters, as well as non-living things such as photographs, Arcanum materials, and technological items, to remain unaffected by the time-regression of The Storm, though it cannot shield humans from regression.

Inside the suitcase is a space far more expansive than its exterior. Under normal circumstances, we chant this incantation to open the suitcase: "Ne iru milde en tiun bonan nokton."

-In a mysterious lake inside the suitcase sits half of an even more mysterious spinning wheel. Wound around the spinning wheel at the center of the lake are imperceptible thread-like filaments; this substance appears to possess a summoning function, and under certain as-yet-unverified circumstances, can summon living beings from a given era here.
-Around the lake, mist hangs thick; those who inhale too much of it (aside from Vertin) can even fall into a coma. The composition of the mist is unknown, and similar mist has been found at both the Apeiron Sanctuary and the Olitiaus Breeding Base.
-According to the Timekeeper's report, she once sensed a presence similar to the spinning wheel on the stones of the ruins of the Apeiron Temple. (This report still lacks further corroborating supplementary evidence.)

notes.title: Hat
notes.text: This is an elegant top hat that suits the vast majority of eras, possessing the same gentleness and resilience as its owner.

notes.title: Nixie Tube Watch
notes.text: A Nixie tube watch developed with assistance from the Laplace Computing Center. According to Laplace personnel who took part in the project, they did not play any major role in the watch's development.

What kind of figure should the protagonist of a game actually be? Does he/she/it possess a certain habitual, almost axiomatic, positive and lively quality? Passionate about everything they experience? Or a hero beloved by all, yearned for by countless people? Those are certainly fine qualities, sensible and taken for granted. Without a doubt, we should stride boldly forward along this path proven by countless stories. Keep at it, colleagues!
The conclusion is obvious—we have no intention of doing that.

Hidden beneath layers of books and a thick layer of silent dust, the caramel color gleams faintly, seeping from the folds of time. This was once a fine jar of toffee. It came from the rough hands of an unknown vendor, whom I happened to bump into while sneaking out from behind the gray walls. The warmth and fragrance hidden within the jar are often remembered, but it will never be opened again.

A dash of "taciturnity," a dash of "bravery," a dash of "practicality," a teaspoon of "gentleness," a smidgen of "volatile passion," and of course, a drop of the indispensable "mischievousness." In a long and arduous process of careful selection, we finally arrived at this ideal protagonist. Of course, we cannot deny the cold sweat and trepidation we felt before the curtain was lifted on stage, and we also unconsciously doubted this bold decision. Fortunately, we persevered. Now, we can proudly say—this is the one and only protagonist of *Reverse: 1999*. We sincerely hope you will enjoy this design, and that the experiences and observations along this journey will bring you a sense of flow and profound emotion.

P.S. As for further details regarding the creative process, the journey is still ongoing, and we cannot elaborate further. We sincerely apologize for any doubts or speculations that may arise. (bows) (dodging chicken leg—)
